chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Muqri, from Yunus ibn Dabyan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites 'Surah Buruj' (The Constellations) in his obligatory prayers, for it is the Surah of the Prophets, his gathering place and standing place will be with the Prophets, the Messengers, and the Righteous.

key_terms.مَحْشَرُهُ: His gathering place (on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Buruj in obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration in *Thawab al-Amal*, emphasizing the intercessory power of Surah Al-Buruj when integrated into obligatory (Fard) prayers. The text explicitly links the reciter's eschatological status to the 'Anbiya' (Prophets), promising a distinguished position among the Messengers and the Righteous (Salihin) on the Day of Resurrection. This reflects the Shia tradition of attributing specific spiritual ranks to the consistent recitation of key Quranic chapters during daily worship.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from al-Hussain b. Ahmad al-Muqri from Yunis b. Dhabyan from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who recites Surah Buruj in his obligatory prayers, by virtue of the dignity of this Surah, he would be raised among the prophets because this Surah is related to them.”
